title: Python Inheritance Quiz
description: Test your understanding of Python class inheritance concepts.

questions.question: What is inheritance in Python OOP?
options: A class deriving attributes and methods from another class
questions.explanation: Inheritance allows a class (child) to access attributes and methods from another class (parent).

questions.question: Which keyword is used to inherit from a parent class?
questions.explanation: Python uses the syntax `class Child(Parent):` to inherit from a parent class.
Class B inherits from A, so it can access A's `show()` method. It prints 'A'.

questions.question: Which function allows access to a parent class method from a child?
questions.explanation: `super()` is used to call parent class methods in a child class.

questions.question:
What type of inheritance is this?

```python
class A: pass
class B(A): pass
class C(B): pass
```
questions.explanation: C inherits from B which inherits from A, forming a multilevel inheritance chain.

questions.question: What type of inheritance allows a child to inherit from multiple parents?
questions.explanation: Multiple inheritance allows a class to inherit from more than one parent class.
Child class B overrides `show()` method of parent A, so it prints 'B'.

questions.question:
What type of inheritance is this?

```python
class A: pass
class B(A): pass
class C(A): pass
```
questions.explanation: Both B and C inherit from A, forming a hierarchical inheritance structure.

questions.question: What happens if a method is not found in the child class?
options: Python searches in the parent class
questions.explanation: If a child class doesn’t have the method, Python looks for it in the parent class(es).

questions.question: Which statement is true about inheritance?
options: Inheritance is only used in functions
Parent classes can access child attributes directly
Child classes can access parent attributes and methods
questions.explanation: Child classes inherit attributes and methods from the parent, enabling code reuse.
